title: Paid time off policy
text: Full-time employees at Kestrel Robotics accrue 22 days of paid time off per year. Unused PTO of up to 5 days carries over to the next calendar year. Requests longer than 10 consecutive days need approval from a department head.

title: Paid time off policy (2023, superseded)
text: This policy was superseded in January 2025. Under the 2023 policy, employees accrued 18 days of PTO per year and could carry over up to 10 unused days.

title: Parental leave
text: Kestrel offers 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to all parents, available within the first year after birth or adoption. The leave can be taken in up to three separate blocks.

title: Sick leave
text: Sick leave is unlimited. Absences longer than 5 working days require a doctor's note submitted to People Operations.

title: Expense policy
text: Expenses must be submitted within 30 days of purchase through Ledgerly. Meals while travelling are reimbursed up to 60 euros per day. Receipts are required for any expense above 25 euros.

title: Booking business travel
text: All flights must be booked through the TripDesk portal. Economy class is required for flights under 6 hours. Premium economy is allowed for flights of 6 hours or longer.

title: Equipment and home office
text: New hires receive a one-time home office stipend of 750 euros. Laptops are provided by IT and must be returned within 14 days of leaving the company.

title: Lisbon office
text: The Lisbon office is the Kestrel headquarters, located at Rua da Prata 120. It hosts the engineering and finance teams and is open from 8:00 to 20:00 on weekdays.

title: Nairobi office
text: The Nairobi office opened in March 2024 in Westlands. It hosts the field operations and customer support teams.

title: Austin office
text: The Austin office houses hardware manufacturing and the drone test range. Visitors must be escorted at all times on the test range.

title: K-200 specifications
text: The K-200 is the Kestrel survey drone. It has a flight time of 42 minutes, a maximum payload of 1.8 kg, and an operating range of 8 km.

title: K-200 battery care
text: The K-200 uses the KB-6 battery pack, which takes 75 minutes to charge fully. Batteries should be stored at 40 to 60 percent charge when not in use for more than a week.

title: K-300 specifications
text: The K-300 is the heavy-lift successor to the K-200, launched in 2025. It carries up to 5 kg with a flight time of 31 minutes.

title: K-200 firmware updates
text: K-200 firmware updates are released monthly. Version 4.2 added obstacle avoidance in low light. Updates must be installed through the Kestrel Fleet app, never over USB.

title: Kestrel Fleet app
text: Kestrel Fleet is the mobile app used to plan missions, install firmware, and download flight logs. It is available on Android and iOS.

title: Drone warranty
text: Kestrel drones have a 2-year limited warranty covering manufacturing defects. Crash damage is not covered unless the customer has purchased CarePlus.

title: CarePlus protection plan
text: CarePlus costs 199 euros per year per drone and covers up to two crash replacements each year, with a 50 euro deductible per claim.

title: Returns and refunds
text: Customers may return unopened products within 30 days for a full refund. Opened products can be returned within 14 days with a 15 percent restocking fee.

title: Customer support hours
text: Customer support is available 24/7 by chat. Phone support runs from 7:00 to 22:00 East Africa Time and is staffed by the Nairobi team.

title: Enterprise support SLA
text: Enterprise customers receive a 4-hour first-response SLA for priority-1 incidents and a next-business-day SLA for all other tickets.

title: Engineering on-call
text: Engineering on-call rotations last one week, starting on Mondays at 10:00 Lisbon time. On-call engineers receive a weekly allowance of 300 euros.

title: Incident severity levels
text: A SEV1 incident is a full outage of Kestrel Fleet or any safety issue with a drone in flight. SEV1 incidents require a public status page update within 30 minutes.

title: Postmortems
text: A written postmortem is required for every SEV1 and SEV2 incident within 5 business days. Postmortems are blameless and are reviewed at the Thursday reliability meeting.

title: Mobile release process
text: Mobile app releases ship every second Tuesday. A release needs sign-off from QA and one engineering manager. Hotfixes may skip the schedule but still need QA sign-off.

title: Code review rules
text: Every pull request needs at least one approving review. Changes to flight-control code need two approvals, one of them from the flight-safety team.

title: Passwords and access
text: A password manager is required for all work accounts. Passwords must be at least 14 characters long, and hardware security keys are mandatory for production access.

title: Reporting security incidents
text: Suspected security incidents must be reported to security@kestrel.example within 1 hour of discovery. Do not attempt to investigate on your own.

title: Flight log retention
text: Customer flight logs are retained for 18 months and then deleted automatically. Customers can request earlier deletion through the Fleet app.

title: Company history
text: Kestrel Robotics was founded in 2019 in Lisbon by Ana Ferreira and Daniel Otieno. The K-200 was its first commercial product, released in 2021.

title: Learning budget
text: Each employee has an annual learning budget of 1,000 euros for courses, books, and conferences. Unused budget does not roll over.
